Subject: Request: technical evidence for 'no-learn' commitments and subprocessor residency

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick conversation yesterday. As part of HealthNova's procurement security review for the pilot (HN-8942), our legal/compliance team needs technical evidence to operationalize the DPA clauses we discussed. Specifically we need:

- A short (one-page) description of how Redwood enforces a "no-learn" / "no-training" commitment for tenant data (technical controls and any deploy-time flags).
- A current list of subprocessors, including country of processing and whether they process content or only infra telemetry.
- Confirmation of EU residency options (which regions, which services can be kept onshore), plus any routing/geo policies we need to configure.
- Example logs/artefacts that prove training data is never persisted for model updates (redacted is OK).

Can you please provide these artifacts within 2 business days? We will attach them to the DPA addendum and the internal risk memo. If you have a prebuilt evidence pack or CSV inventory, that would be ideal.

Also: does Redwood have a standard statement we can include in the DPA about prompt/response ownership? Our legal team is looking for a single-sentence representation that customers retain ownership of prompts and responses and Redwood will not use them to improve models.

Appreciate your help — Sophie

--

Sophie — attaching the evidence pack and a current subprocessor inventory. High level answers below; the attachments contain logs, configuration snippets, and the CSV you requested.

Summary (short):
- No-train enforcement: tenant data sent to Redwood inference endpoints is tagged with a per-tenant metadata flag at ingest. By default, the flag sets "no_training=true" for hosted and dedicated customers who opt into the no-learn DPA. Our serving runtime treats that flag as authoritative: telemetry collection (model telemetry and metrics) strips user content, and persistent model update pipelines ignore any inputs marked with no_training.

- Technical controls:
  * Ingest pipeline flagging (implementation: request header X-Redwood-No-Train: true; API and SDKs set at client config).
  * Persistent storage: prompt/response content is stored only in ephemeral KV caches for the duration of the session unless the customer chooses to persist logs; by default we retain ephemeral content for up to 24 hours then delete.
  * Training pipelines: separate closed pipelines used for model improvement require explicit export via an internal approval workflow; no tenant-tagged data flows into those pipelines unless the approval gate is exercised (not available for customers who opt-in to no-train).
  * Runtime enforcement: inference nodes enforce an allowlist so that nodes designated for "no-train" customers never export tensors or caches to long-term training stores.

- Subprocessors & residency: see attached CSV (subprocessor_inventory_apr2028.csv). Short answers: EU onshore options available (Frankfurt eu-central-1 and Dublin eu-west-1 deployments). Customers can choose the EU-only routing policy; in that mode all processing (ingest, inference, ephemeral KV) occurs in the selected region and logs are stored onshore. Where we use cloud providers for GPU hosts, subprocessors are listed with the nature of access (compute-only vs. content-processing).

- Evidence artefacts attached:
  1) redwood-no-learn-evidence-pack.pdf — contains architecture diagrams, sample config lines (X-Redwood-No-Train header), redacted log excerpts showing anonymized request IDs and absence of content in model-update store, and an ops checklist for audits.
  2) subprocessor_inventory_apr2028.csv — current list of subprocessors, data types processed, and countries.
  3) redwood-technical-architecture-diagram.png — simplified diagram showing the separation between inference runtime and model improvement pipelines.

Quick note on prompt/response ownership language you asked for:
- Draft sentence: "Customer retains exclusive ownership of prompts and responses; Redwood will not use customer prompts or responses to improve or retrain any models for any purpose unless Customer provides explicit, written consent."

That sentence reflects our operational configuration for no-train customers and is the wording our legal team prefers to include in the DPA addendum. Marissa — if you have edits for procurement-friendly phrasing, please suggest.

If you'd like, we can also provide a signed attestation on company letterhead.

Includes forwarding of Sophie's original request below.

Attachments: redwood-no-learn-evidence-pack.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB); subprocessor_inventory_apr2028.csv (CSV, 24KB); redwood-technical-architecture-diagram.png (PNG, 210KB)

Dev / Irene —

Thank you, that package is extremely helpful and covers most of our asks. Two quick follow-ups before I circulate to our risk committee:

1) Export controls / derived works: does Redwood consider model outputs (responses) to be derivative works of your underlying models such that Redwood claims any rights or licences over them? We want a sentence confirming that HealthNova retains full rights to outputs generated by our inputs.

2) Attestation: we'd appreciate the signed company attestation you mentioned if that's straightforward — that gives procurement the strongest evidence for the DPA file.

If you can provide short affirmative wording for (1) and a PDF attestation for (2) we'll be ready to proceed with the addendum.

Best,
